latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* test(generic): support pandas 3.1 timedelta expectations by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/895
* fix(indicators): select unmapped input columns by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/889
* fix(data): initialize download kwargs in from_data by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/890
* fix(utils): preserve dictionary state on rejected loads by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/891
* fix(records): pass group_by to top_n and bottom_n masks by @wavebyrd in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/892
* Fix single-column DataFrame outputs from pandas-ta by @Don-Yin in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/893
* fix(data): preserve named Series in column alignment by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/898
* fix(generic): prevent narrow integer diff overflow by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/899
* fix(returns): return NaN or signed infinity for zero-volatility Sharpe and Sortino by @ryanduguid in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/897
* perf(generic): O(n) rolling min/max using a monotonic deque by @destinyN1 in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/901
* fix(indicators): avoid unsigned true range underflow by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/900
* test(utils): keep invalid timezone fixture compatible with dateparser by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/907
* fix(base): align reordered equal-length indexes by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/905
* fix(generic): handle nonpositive diff periods by @JohnDReynolds in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/906
* fix(portfolio): stop dropping a lot when flooring to size_granularity by @stooq1 in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/894
* feat(generic): add crossed_below_1d_nb and crossed_below_nb by @20163070 in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/908
* fix(records): respect group_by in MappedArray.describe on pandas 3 by @wavebyrd in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/910
* Expose type hints by @Dreamsorcerer in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/844
* fix(portfolio): divide gross exposure by portfolio value by @stooq1 in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/903
* fix(returns): treat constant returns as zero volatility in Sharpe ratio by @gautamggg53 in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/904
* Improve index-alignment and true-range performance while preserving validation and integer precision by @polakowo
* Consolidate regression tests and include shared test helpers in source distributions by @polakowo
* Expand documentation walkthroughs, add interactive charts, and refresh README examples and visuals by @polakowo

## New Contributors
* @Don-Yin made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/893
* @ryanduguid made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/897
* @destinyN1 made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/901
* @stooq1 made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/894
* @20163070 made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/908
* @Dreamsorcerer made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/844
* @gautamggg53 made their first contribution in https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/pull/904

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.1

简体中文 / English | Features · Installation · Examples · Links

Trading research at scale.

VectorBT is a Python toolkit for trading research. Explore market data, build indicators and signals, and compare thousands of ideas across assets and timeframes. NumPy arrays, Numba acceleration, and an optional Rust engine let you run large experiments in a few lines of Python.

--- Move from exploring price patterns to evaluating strategies in one workflow. Inspect trades, fees, drawdowns, and portfolio performance, then explore the results with interactive charts. Built for traders, researchers, and AI agents, VectorBT brings data analysis, strategy simulation, and visualization together in a composable Python API. VectorBT is the open-source community edition of [VectorBT PRO](https://vectorbt.pro/). PRO extends the library with parallelization, additional data integrations, portfolio optimization, pattern recognition, event projections, limit orders, leverage, and over 100 other features, with new features added weekly. See [VectorBT vs PRO](https://vectorbt.dev/getting-started/upgrade/) or browse [PRO feature examples](https://vectorbt.pro/features/). ## Features

Fast, vectorized backtesting

Research strategies at scale with pandas, NumPy, and Numba.

Backtesting examples →

Optional Rust engine

Use precompiled kernels for supported operations without JIT compilation.

Rust engine →

Pandas-native API

Work with custom accessors and high-performance operations directly on pandas objects.

Pandas integration →

Flexible broadcasting

Analyze multiple assets and sweep large parameter grids with flexible array broadcasting.

Broadcasting API →

Rich indicator ecosystem

Build custom indicators and use integrations for TA-Lib, Pandas TA, and more.

Indicator features →

Portfolio backtesting

Analyze trades, drawdowns, and performance, with QuantStats integration.

Portfolio analysis →

Signal tooling

Generate, rank, map, and analyze the distribution of trading signals.

Signal features →

Built-in data access

Fetch market data, preprocess it, and generate synthetic time series.

Data features →

Robustness testing

Run walk-forward optimization and generate labels for machine learning workflows.

Robustness testing →

Interactive visualization

Explore results with Plotly charts, Jupyter widgets, and browser dashboards.

Plotting features →

Automation tools

Schedule data updates and send Telegram notifications.

Scheduling and notifications →

Composable Python API

Combine building blocks for rapid experimentation and AI agent-driven workflows.

Python workflows →
## Installation ```sh pip install -U vectorbt ``` To install the optional Rust engine: ```sh pip install -U "vectorbt[rust]" ``` To install all optional integrations (TA-Lib, Pandas TA, etc.): ```sh pip install -U "vectorbt[full]" ``` To install all optional integrations together with the Rust engine: ```sh pip install -U "vectorbt[full,rust]" ``` ## Examples ### Invest $100 in Bitcoin since 2014 ```python import vectorbt as vbt data = vbt.YFData.download("BTC-USD") price = data.get("Close") pf = vbt.Portfolio.from_holding(price, init_cash=100) print(pf.total_profit()) ``` Output: ```text 19501.10906763755 ``` ### Trade a dual-SMA crossover strategy ```python fast_ma = vbt.MA.run(price, 10) slow_ma = vbt.MA.run(price, 50) entries = fast_ma.ma_crossed_above(slow_ma) exits = fast_ma.ma_crossed_below(slow_ma) pf = vbt.Portfolio.from_signals(price, entries, exits, init_cash=100) print(pf.total_profit()) ``` Output: ```text 34417.80960086067 ``` > [!TIP] > **VectorBT PRO** > > Simulate [limit orders](https://vectorbt.pro/features/backtesting/orders-and-execution/#limit-orders), > use [leverage](https://vectorbt.pro/features/backtesting/fees-slippage-and-leverage/#leverage), and model futures with > [contract multipliers](https://vectorbt.pro/features/backtesting/fees-slippage-and-leverage/#contract-multiplier). ### Generate 1,000 random strategies ```python import numpy as np symbols = ["BTC-USD", "ETH-USD"] data = vbt.YFData.download(symbols, missing_index="drop") price = data.get("Close") n = np.random.randint(10, 101, size=1000).tolist() pf = vbt.Portfolio.from_random_signals(price, n=n, init_cash=100, seed=42) mean_expectancy = pf.trades.expectancy().groupby(["randnx_n", "symbol"]).mean() fig = mean_expectancy.unstack().vbt.scatterplot(xaxis_title="randnx_n", yaxis_title="mean_expectancy") fig.show() ``` Output: ### Test 10,000 dual-SMA window combinations ```python symbols = ["BTC-USD", "ETH-USD", "XRP-USD"] data = vbt.YFData.download(symbols, missing_index="drop") price = data.get("Close") windows = np.arange(2, 101) fast_ma, slow_ma = vbt.MA.run_combs(price, window=windows, r=2, short_names=["fast", "slow"]) entries = fast_ma.ma_crossed_above(slow_ma) exits = fast_ma.ma_crossed_below(slow_ma) pf = vbt.Portfolio.from_signals(price, entries, exits, size=np.inf, fees=0.001, freq="1D") fig = pf.total_return().vbt.heatmap( x_level="fast_window", y_level="slow_window", slider_level="symbol", symmetric=True, trace_kwargs=dict(colorbar=dict(title="Total return", tickformat="%")), ) fig.show() ``` Output: > [!TIP] > **VectorBT PRO** > > Use [random search](https://vectorbt.pro/features/optimization/strategy-optimization/#random-search) to sample a large > parameter grid, or [conditional parameters](https://vectorbt.pro/features/optimization/strategy-optimization/#conditional-parameters) > to exclude combinations such as a fast MA window longer than the slow MA window. The > [cross-validation tutorial](https://vectorbt.pro/tutorials/cross-validation/) > shows how to select parameters on training data and evaluate them on later periods. ### Inspect any strategy configuration ```python print(pf[(10, 20, "ETH-USD")].stats()) ``` Output: ```text Start 2017-11-09 00:00:00+00:00 End 2026-01-03 00:00:00+00:00 Period 2978 days 00:00:00 Start Value 100.0 End Value 1604.093789 Total Return [%] 1504.093789 Benchmark Return [%] 866.094127 Max Gross Exposure [%] 100.0 Total Fees Paid 204.226289 Max Drawdown [%] 70.734951 Max Drawdown Duration 1095 days 00:00:00 Total Trades 81 Total Closed Trades 80 Total Open Trades 1 Open Trade PnL -14.232533 Win Rate [%] 41.25 Best Trade [%] 120.511071 Worst Trade [%] -27.772271 Avg Winning Trade [%] 27.265519 Avg Losing Trade [%] -9.022864 Avg Winning Trade Duration 32 days 20:21:49.090909091 Avg Losing Trade Duration 8 days 16:51:03.829787234 Profit Factor 1.275515 Expectancy 18.979079 Sharpe Ratio 0.861945 Calmar Ratio 0.572758 Omega Ratio 1.20277 Sortino Ratio 1.301377 Name: (10, 20, ETH-USD), dtype: object ``` ### Plot any strategy configuration ```python pf[(10, 20, "ETH-USD")].plot().show() ``` Output: ### Animate Bollinger Bands across multiple symbols VectorBT goes beyond backtesting, with tools for financial data analysis and visualization: ```python symbols = ["BTC-USD", "ETH-USD", "XRP-USD"] data = vbt.YFData.download(symbols, period="6mo", missing_index="drop") price = data.get("Close") bbands = vbt.BBANDS.run(price) def plot(index, bbands): bbands = bbands.loc[index] fig = vbt.make_subplots( rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.15, subplot_titles=("%B", "Bandwidth") ) fig.update_layout(showlegend=False, width=750, height=400) bbands.percent_b.vbt.ts_heatmap( trace_kwargs=dict( zmin=0, zmid=0.5, zmax=1, colorscale="Spectral", colorbar=dict(y=(fig.layout.yaxis.domain[0] + fig.layout.yaxis.domain[1]) / 2, len=0.5), ), add_trace_kwargs=dict(row=1, col=1), fig=fig, ) bbands.bandwidth.vbt.ts_heatmap( trace_kwargs=dict(colorbar=dict(y=(fig.layout.yaxis2.domain[0] + fig.layout.yaxis2.domain[1]) / 2, len=0.5)), add_trace_kwargs=dict(row=2, col=1), fig=fig, ) return fig vbt.save_animation( "bbands.gif", bbands.wrapper.index, plot, bbands, delta=90, step=3, fps=3, writer_kwargs=dict(loop=0) ) ``` Output: ```text 100%|██████████| 31/31 [00:21<00:00, 1.21it/s] ``` Visit the [website](https://vectorbt.dev/) for more examples, documentation, and guides. ## Example apps ### [Candlestick Patterns](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/blob/master/apps/candlestick-patterns/) Explore candlestick patterns interactively and backtest their signals with VectorBT. ## Links * [Website](https://vectorbt.dev/) * [Docker images](https://hub.docker.com/r/polakowo/vectorbt) * [Colab notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1ibqyrf6LPFlzRb6mkPpl3hxqL6ryNBXI?usp=sharing) ## License This work is [fair-code](http://faircode.io/) distributed under the [Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause](https://github.com/polakowo/vectorbt/blob/master/LICENSE.md) license. The source code is publicly available, and everyone (individuals and organizations) may use it for free. However, you may not sell products or services that are primarily this software. If you have questions or want to request a license exception, please [contact the author](mailto:olegpolakow@vectorbt.pro). Installing optional dependencies may be subject to a more restrictive license. ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who has contributed to VectorBT! ## Star History ## Disclaimer This software is for educational purposes only. Do not risk money you cannot afford to lose. Use the software at your own risk. The authors and affiliates assume no responsibility for your trading results.

简体中文 / English | 功能 · 安装 · 示例 · 链接

让交易研究规模化。

VectorBT 是面向交易研究的 Python 工具库。探索市场数据，构建指标和信号，跨资产、跨时间周期比较数千种交易思路。借助 NumPy 数组、Numba 加速和可选的 Rust 引擎，只需几行 Python 代码即可开展大规模实验。

--- 在同一工作流中，从探索价格形态到评估交易策略。查看交易、费用、回撤和投资组合表现，并通过交互式图表分析结果。VectorBT 面向交易者、研究人员和 AI 智能体，通过可组合的 Python API 将数据分析、策略模拟和可视化整合在一起。 VectorBT 是 [VectorBT PRO](https://vectorbt.pro/) 的开源社区版。 PRO 在此基础上提供并行计算、更多数据集成、投资组合优化、形态识别、事件预测、限价单、杠杆等功能， 以及其他 100 多项功能，并且每周持续新增功能。 查看 [VectorBT 与 PRO 的对比](https://vectorbt.dev/getting-started/upgrade/)，或浏览 [PRO 功能示例](https://vectorbt.pro/features/)。 ## 功能

高速向量化回测

基于 pandas、NumPy 和 Numba，开展大规模策略研究。

回测示例 →

可选的 Rust 引擎

为支持的运算提供预编译内核，无需承担 JIT 编译开销。

Rust 引擎 →

原生集成 pandas 的 API

通过自定义访问器，直接对 pandas 对象执行高性能运算。

pandas 集成 →

灵活的广播机制

利用灵活的数组广播，开展多资产分析和大规模参数扫描。

广播 API →

丰富的指标生态

构建自定义指标，并使用 TA-Lib、Pandas TA 等工具集成。

指标功能 →

分析交易、回撤和绩效，并集成 QuantStats。

投资组合分析 →

信号工具

生成、排序和映射交易信号，并分析其分布。

信号功能 →

获取市场数据、执行预处理，并生成合成时间序列。

绘图功能 →

定时更新数据，并发送 Telegram 通知。

定时任务与通知 →

可组合的 Python API

组合功能模块，支持快速实验和由 AI 智能体驱动的工作流。

Python 工作流 →

install -U "vectorbt[full,rust]" ``` ## 示例 ### 从 2014 年起向比特币投资 100 美元 ```python import vectorbt as vbt data = vbt.YFData.download("BTC-USD") price = data.get("Close") pf =
